Components / Surfaces

Row panel

.dr-rows · __row · __key · __val · __row--stack · components/rows.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Delivered toOsokorky, 14
Time10:07
OperatorAndriy M.
  1. 1.dr-rowsThe panel: --bg-surface, radius 16, padding 8 / 16. A grid whose label column is sized by the widest key in this panel, floored at 96.
  2. 2.dr-rows__rowOne fact, 13px 0, with a hairline under it and none under the last. Each row is a subgrid of the panel, so every value in the card starts on one axis.
  3. 3.dr-rows__keyThe label, 13/400 in --text-muted, 5.95:1.
  4. 4.dr-rows__valThe value, 15/600 in --text-primary, tabular, 14.37:1, reading from the left after a 10 gap.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Row panel.

States

No state of its own: its rows are facts to read, and nothing in it takes focus.

When to use

The row panel is the system's universal container for a fact: read, opened, or typed into. It stands on 61 files, among them tracking, delivery, order-confirmed, order-review, inspection-report, job-brief, earning-details and account-edit, where the same grid holds fields and picker rows. The same component on two screens carries the same numbers.

Values read from the left on the card's own axis. HIG ships both a trailing value (HIG · Lists and tables) and a leading one (HIG · Text fields), so this is a taste call and not a compliance fix; WCAG 1.4.3, 1.3.1 and 1.4.8 are untouched. Inside a titled zone card the panel gives up its ground and bleeds −16, so its separators run 16 / 16 from the card's edges.

The key is the dictionary noun for the fact (Delivered to, Operator, never Pilot); the value is the fact itself, a place, a time, a name. No adjectives and no sentence in a value.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Row panel · inventory.md § 1.3 (Row panel) · voice.md Vocabulary · ui/kit.html Row panel

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Delivered toOsokorky, 14
Time10:07
OperatorAndriy M.

The delivery details on delivery: where, when, who. Three facts, one card, one value axis.

Don’t

Delivered toOsokorky, 14
Time10:07

One card per fact. Each pair becomes an object of its own and the reader loses the value axis. Put the facts as rows in one panel. For a price broken into its parts use money rows; for a list of objects use cards in a list.
